name: Zendesk
summary: Zendesk provides customer support, ticketing, and integration APIs. OAuth2 is the recommended authentication method for apps, integrations, and bots, especially if they will be distributed to multiple Zendesk customers. For private or internal integrations, developers may use regular OAuth apps. Composio offers a managed OAuth option for Zendesk, or users can set up their own OAuth credentials.
decision: You can use either Composio's managed OAuth for Zendesk or set up your own custom Zendesk OAuth credentials if you need more control or plan to distribute your integration. Follow the link to the Composio Zendesk OAuth credential creation guide if you choose bring-your-own. For distributing an app to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use a global OAuth client as per Zendesk's guidelines.

auth_type.note: Zendesk supports OAuth2 as the primary authentication method for apps and integrations.

prerequisites.title: Zendesk Account with Appropriate Plan
prerequisites.body: You need a Zendesk account with the Suite Growth plan or above, or Support Professional plan or above.

prerequisites.title: Admin Access
prerequisites.body: You must be an admin or have access to an admin in your Zendesk account.

prerequisites.title: Zendesk Command Line Interface (ZCLI)
prerequisites.body: Install the Zendesk CLI (ZCLI) for app development and management.
prerequisites.note: ZCLI is used to initialize, run, and test your Zendesk app.

prerequisites.title: Familiarity with OAuth2
prerequisites.body: You should understand basic OAuth2 concepts including authorization flows and access tokens.

steps.title: Decide on Managed or Own OAuth
steps.body: Choose whether to use Composio-managed OAuth (simpler setup, no client registration needed) or register your own Zendesk OAuth credentials (needed for more control or broad distribution).

steps.title: If bringing your own, register an OAuth client in Zendesk
steps.body: Create an OAuth client in Zendesk Admin Center. Use the required redirect URI: https://zis.zendesk.com/api/services/zis/connections/oauth/callback

steps.title: Save the OAuth client details securely
steps.body: Store the client ID and client secret securely as you will need them for your app or integration configuration.

steps.title: Configure OAuth credentials in the app
steps.body: Add the OAuth client ID, client secret, authorization URI, and token URI to your application's configuration or manifest file.

steps.title: Authenticate and authorize the app
steps.body: Follow the OAuth flow using the configured app. Admin users will grant permissions, and the resulting access token can be used for API requests.

human_actions.title: Choose between managed OAuth and own credentials
human_actions.body: The person setting up the integration must decide whether to use Composio-managed OAuth or their own Zendesk OAuth app.

human_actions.title: Register an OAuth app in Zendesk (if bringing your own)
human_actions.body: Use Zendesk Admin Center to create an OAuth client if not using Composio-managed OAuth.

human_actions.title: Enter credentials in configuration
human_actions.body: Input the saved client ID and secret into your application or service configuration.

human_actions.title: Grant OAuth consent via Zendesk
human_actions.body: A Zendesk admin grants permissions to the OAuth app during the authorization step.
